topic.title: Test is 100% timsTOF, train is 46%: a train/test shift checklist before you build a reference library
topic.forumName: Enveda CASMI 2026 - Molecule ID From Mass Spectra
topic.content:
I compared the metadata of the current train.parquet with the visible test.parquet. The spectra arrays aren't needed for any of this. A few differences matter for anyone building a retrieval library or training on train:

train (2.54M spectra, 276k molecules) visible test (1,213 spectra, 400 molecules)
Instrument 46% timsTOF, 30% Orbitrap, the rest QTOF / ion trap / QqQ 100% timsTOF
Adducts 52% [M+H]+, 18% [M-H]-, 13% dimers ([2M+Na]+, [2M+H]+, [2M-H]-) 79% [M+H]+, 16% [M-H]-, no dimers
Precursor m/z median 350, but min 2 and max ~2.4 million 245–460, median 329
Collision energy same energies written as 60, 60.0 and [60.0] clean 20 / 40 / 60 and stepped 20,40,60 (plus negatives)

What I'd do with it:

  1. Weight or filter by instrument. Fragmentation differs between Orbitrap (HCD) and timsTOF (CID), so a timsTOF-only (or timsTOF-weighted) reference set is probably a better match for test. Instrument names come in ~15 spellings (QTOF, qTof, qtof, LC-ESI-QTOF, …), so normalise them first.
  2. Drop dimer adducts from the library, or at least from the candidate ranking. None of them appear in test.
  3. Drop impossible precursors. Anything outside roughly 50–2,000 m/z is a unit or parsing error.
  4. Parse collision energy into numbers before using it as a feature. Otherwise 60, 60.0 and [60.0] look like three different settings.
  5. Build CV from the same slice: positive and negative mode in about the test's 80/20 ratio, [M+H]+ / [M-H]- dominant, with precursors 240–470. And split by inchikey14, never by spectrum, or the same molecule ends up on both sides.

One caveat: this is the visible test file. The hidden test used at scoring may be larger, but a code competition's visible test is usually drawn the same way.

Numbers come from a metadata-only script (no spectra loaded). Happy to share it if useful, and if you've seen the timsTOF-only subset help or hurt your CV, I'd like to hear it.
